description: Disallow exec. Common on /tmp, /var, /home for hardening.
Ignore setuid/setgid. Hardening for /tmp, /home, container rootfs.
Block device-node access. Container rootfs always nodev.
Update atime only if older than mtime/ctime or > 24h. The modern default.
Strict POSIX atime semantics. Rarely needed.
Update timestamp in memory; flush only on stat/sync/fdatasync. Reduces metadata writes.
All IO synchronously (huge perf hit; data integrity for removable media).
Sync metadata dir ops (rename, link, unlink, ...).
Mount with mount -a (default for fstab entries).
Skip on mount -a. Mount on demand only.
Data written before metadata (default). Crash-safe but slower than writeback.
Data + metadata async. Fastest; can leak data after crash (stale blocks visible).
Full data journaling. Strongest crash consistency, slowest.
Use write barriers for ordering (correctness). Default.
Disable barriers. Faster but unsafe except on battery-backed cache controllers.
Issue TRIM on every delete (vs periodic fstrim).
Direct IO without inode lock. Helps parallel-DIO workloads (databases).
Allow inodes anywhere on FS (default ≥3.7). inode32 = first 1TB only (legacy 32-bit compat).
Disable quotas (XFS is quota-on by default if mkfs.xfs included).
Read-only base layer(s). Multiple : separated; first wins.
Empty dir on same FS as upperdir for atomic ops.
Allow renaming dirs across overlays via redirect xattr.
Copy only metadata on first write (vs full file). Saves space when only chmod/chown.
Stable inode numbers across overlay layers.
Use user.* xattrs (vs trusted.*) — required for unprivileged overlay (rootless).
No fsync (faster, data lost on crash). Used by ephemeral container layers.
Index dir for upper-lower hard-link tracking. Required for metacopy/redirect.
Max FS size. Suffix %. e.g. size=1G or size=10%.
NUMA mempolicy: default, prefer, bind, interleave, local.
Force compression even on incompressible files.
TRIM. async = batched TRIM (less perf hit).
Allow mount with missing devices (RAID degraded).
Disable COW for new files (existing unchanged). For databases that don't want btrfs COW interfering.
System memory snapshot: MemTotal, MemFree, MemAvailable, Buffers, Cached, SwapTotal, SwapFree, Slab, etc.
Per-CPU info: model name, MHz, cache, flags.
1/5/15min load avg + running/total tasks + last PID.
Major:Minor + size + name of all partitions.
Kernel symbol table (CAP_SYSLOG to see addresses).
Per-process status (state, UIDs, threads, mem, signal masks, caps).
Per-process IO counters (rchar, wchar, syscr, syscw, read_bytes, write_bytes, cancelled_write_bytes).
Active IO scheduler. Selectable values in [brackets]: mq-deadline, kyber, bfq, none.
Per-queue request depth. Higher = more parallelism, higher latency tail.
Read-ahead window. 0 disables; databases often set 0 or low.
Create if missing. Requires mode arg.
With O_CREAT: fail if exists. Atomic 'create-only'.
Don't make terminal a controlling tty.
Non-blocking mode (read returns EAGAIN if no data).
Synchronous IO — write returns only after data on disk.
Bypass page cache. Buffer + size alignment required.
Don't update atime on this open.
Close FD on execve. Always-set when atomicity matters (otherwise race with fork+exec).
Open as 'reference only' — no read/write, but usable for *at(dirfd, ...) syscalls. Lower-overhead than full open.
Create unnamed temp file. Made permanent via linkat with AT_EMPTY_PATH. Race-free secure-tmp pattern.
Forbid escaping below dirfd (no .. traversal above).
Treat dirfd as root (chroot-like, but per-call). Magic for safe container fs operations.
Only succeed if all dentries cached (fast-path; for nginx-like 'open file or punt').
Writable file closed. The 'edit done' signal.
Event queue overflowed (events lost — bump fs.inotify.max_queued_events).
Permission event for OPEN — kernel waits for ALLOW/DENY.
Kernel polls SQ — userspace doesn't need io_uring_enter syscall on submit.
Device. UUID=, LABEL=, /dev/<name>, or //server/share for CIFS.
fsck pass order. 0 = skip; 1 = root; 2+ = others (parallel within same number).
User-controlled xattrs. Anyone with write access.
Security modules: SELinux (security.selinux), file capabilities (security.capability), IMA (security.ima).
Root-only. Used by docker/runc for storage driver state.
Mask — caps effective permissions of named entries (named-user/group + non-owner group).
Default ACL inherited by new files in directory.
Pass TRIM through to underlying device. Information leak vs perf trade-off.
File type + permissions. S_IFMT mask + S_IFREG/DIR/LNK/BLK/CHR/FIFO/SOCK + mode bits.
Logical size in bytes (sparse files: > st_blocks*512).
Disk usage in 512B blocks (real on-disk space).
Hard link count. 0 = file deleted (still open via FDs).
FS magic number (0xEF53 ext4, 0x58465342 XFS, 0x9123683E btrfs, 0x01021994 tmpfs, 0x9P2000 9p, etc.).
Free blocks available to non-root (excludes reserved).
Mount flag bits (ST_RDONLY, ST_NOSUID, ST_NODEV, ST_NOEXEC, etc.).
Max symlinks followed in path resolution before ELOOP.
chattr flags: immutable, append-only, no-atime, journal-data, compress, etc.
